FL-069.label: The core tools every modern harness has: files, terminal, Chrome, skills, changing models, compaction (our own take), and interactions with common apps, taken from the most modular standard source.
FL-069.walk: Ask the agent to read a file, run a terminal command, open a page in the browser and use a skill; each works.
FL-069.observed: The live model read the fixture file, ran pwd, navigated and read the local test page, and loaded the project skill. The first combined prompt mixed up the labels. Separate tool results and the final skill run establish each action.

FL-070.label: Image input: paste an image and the agent reviews it.
FL-070.walk: Paste an image; the agent reviews it.
FL-070.observed: The browser pasted an image through the clipboard. The model named the red A7 circle and blue B2 square in the answer.

FL-075.label: Queuing prompts and interjecting or steering a running agent, like the modern harnesses do.
FL-075.walk: Queue a prompt during a run and interject once; the queued prompt runs after and the interjection steers the run.
FL-075.observed: Queued a second prompt and steered the active run. The journal recorded STEERED-CEDAR and QUEUED-COPPER and the queued work ran after the first response.

FL-098.label: The symphony lifecycle shows its human touchpoints, the human prompt and any interjection or steering, so they can be seen.
FL-098.walk: Steer a symphony mid-run; the human prompt and the steering both show on the run's trace.
FL-098.observed: The signed run shows the original request, the human follow-up asking for Cedar and its steering acknowledgement. The run persisted the same follow-up.

FL-100.label: Constitution: "Take this to a symphony" from chat, returning as a card. (chat 2026-08-17 17:02:48)
FL-100.walk: Type "take this to a symphony" in chat; the run starts and returns as a card on the Deck.
FL-100.observed: Typed the literal trigger, signed the charge and observed the completed return card in the focused conversation. The returned Symphony card was not independently identified on the Deck.

FL-102.label: The Deck: a flashcard stack of terminals, cards colored to match their agents, only one card on top at a time (that project's agent's last response) to interact with, the next card popping up once you respond, ordered purely by which finished first.
FL-102.walk: Answer the top card; it pops and the next card, the earliest to finish, comes up in its agent's color.
FL-102.observed: Enter removed the single primary card and promoted the previous second card. Its edge remained #94dfbf after promotion. The before/after ordered card IDs and colors are in icons-deck.json.

FL-104.label: A draft response to the final synthesis that you tweak and fire, after which the stack switches to the agent that has waited longest for your attention.
FL-104.walk: Tweak the draft on the top card and fire it; the stack moves to the agent that has waited longest.
FL-104.observed: Edited the top card and fired it. The second card became first and the remaining IDs stayed in order, as recorded in actions.json.

FL-109.label: Memory candidates appear under the agent's post on the Deck after a compaction or a thread close; scrolling past without denying approves them; corpus-born proposals live in Memory Ingest.
FL-109.walk: After a compaction, candidates appear under the post; scroll past; they are approved and land.
FL-109.observed: Ran /compact keep 5 and /compact on a live thread. Compaction reduced 2309 tokens to 962. No candidate cards appeared to scroll past or verify as approved.

FL-114.label: Memory Ingest as its own module: put in current AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files to jump-start the Palace.
FL-114.walk: Put an AGENTS.md into the Memory Ingest module; its contents show up as memory candidates.
FL-114.observed: Uploaded a fixture AGENTS.md through Memory Ingest. A proposed Silverbirch fact appeared for review.

FL-117.label: A proposed reply prefilled and editable; queued prompts advance on Enter with a scrollable queue.
FL-117.walk: Press Enter in the prefilled proposed reply; the next queued prompt comes up and the queue scrolls.
FL-117.observed: The untouched top proposal contained eight characters. Pressing Enter fired it and moved the previous second card into the visible primary slot. icons-deck.json records both positions.

FL-120.label: One conversation module with stack and focused modes.
FL-120.walk: Toggle the conversation module between stack and focused; the one module shows the stack or a single thread.
FL-120.observed: Toggled the conversation module into Deck, inspected the stacked proposals and a secondary reply reader, then returned to the focused journal.

FL-184.label: A distinct module for scheduled jobs that makes them easy to monitor; the best visualization is still to be worked out.
FL-184.walk: Open the scheduled-jobs module; every scheduled job is listed with its current state.
FL-184.observed: Saved one enabled future schedule in the isolated home. The Jobs module listed Library schedule check, its next run and Ready state.

FL-187.label: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
FL-187.walk: List the repositories; the spine and the Harness are two separate git repos.
FL-187.observed: The workspace contains separate Harness and Memory Git roots and origins. impact/repositories.json records their actual Git identities. The image shows the running paired install.

FL-190.label: The Harness can use skills and has the best and most common tools available, compiled from a list.
FL-190.walk: Ask the agent to use a skill in a thread; it loads the skill and follows it.
FL-190.observed: The model loaded read-library-label and read the named local file. The resulting answer contained the expected token CARD-LILAC-72 after a first attempt confused the browser and file labels.

FL-191.label: The tools and skills Claude Code and Codex use on this machine, pinned to versioned open-source sources.
FL-191.walk: Open the tool inventory; each tool or skill lists the versioned open-source source it is pinned to.
FL-191.observed: The open tool inventory listed its versioned upstream tool sources and the discovered local skill revision. The inventory trace retains the list and source links.

FL-194.label: The Pydantic toolset and skills as the tool layer.
FL-194.walk: Open the agent's tool list in a thread; the tools come from the Pydantic toolset plus skills, not from pi.
FL-194.observed: The thread inventory showed tools backed by pinned Pydantic sources and the discovered project skill. The model invoked both types in the walk.

FL-199.label: Icons on buttons for the common things people would understand: a button whose meaning has a known icon (send, stop, add, remove, delete, refresh, open, settings, play, pause) carries it; primary actions show icon and word, row actions the icon alone with a tip; unusual actions keep their word; one icon set across every module and theme.
FL-199.walk: Open any module; every common action (send, stop, add, remove, delete, refresh, open, settings, play, pause) has its icon from the one set in the theme's ink; primary buttons pair it with a word; row actions show the icon alone with a tip; an unusual action still reads as a word.
FL-199.observed: Inspected actual shared controls in seven themes and the speech controls during playback. The complete action-by-action icon, word and tooltip inventory was not established.

FL-201.label: One scale across modules: an icon reused anywhere is one size, text of one role is one size and one font, and a box belongs only to an icon that is a button.
FL-201.walk: Measure every module: each reused icon renders at one size, each text role (module header, row label, body, caption, tip) at one size and font; markers and status glyphs stand bare, only icon buttons are boxed.
FL-201.observed: Sampled rendered styles across modules and captured the module views. The sample does not establish a common size and font for every role. The existing typography flag covers the open comparison.

FL-205.label: The thread list tells you where and how: each thread shows its project by name and the model and thinking level in force, and the list reads cleaner.
FL-205.walk: Open the thread list with threads in two projects on two models: each row names its project (not a path), its model and thinking level, with the same marks wherever that thread is named (the Deck, the conversation header); nothing repeats, nothing truncates.
FL-205.observed: Focused and Deck views showed the pinned model. Two different chat models could not be exercised within the single-model charge.

FL-009.label: Record files (history, transcripts) live apart from code so code can be deleted and re-downloaded without losing history.
FL-009.walk: Delete the code folder, reinstall, `nocturne up`; every thread is still there.
FL-009.observed: The packaged code used for the walk was removed. Reinstalling both wheels and running nocturne up against the same disposable home restored the journal and all 19 thread IDs. The two catalogs are in impact/.

FL-118.label: Out Loud mode: responses are read aloud and listen-triggered dictation is a primary way in, equal to typing, not an add-on.
FL-118.walk: Toggle Out Loud; the answer is spoken; dictation fills the composer and sends on the trigger word.
FL-118.observed: Owner walk: enable Out Loud, grant microphone permission, speak a request and its send word, listen at 1x then 2x and 3x, and speak again after playback. The muted native walk measured speech and the UI canon simulated dictation and listen-after-reading. Hearing and a physical microphone remain open.

FL-170.label: A fresh reinstall that reconnects to existing files and auto-finds the cloud palace.
FL-170.walk: Reinstall on the same machine and run the start command; it finds the existing cloud Palace and the old threads without being told where they are.
FL-170.observed: Performed the same-machine reinstall on a disposable local Palace. Discovery and recovery of the owner's cloud Palace require a different authorized account or deployment.

FL-186.label: Build on Pydantic AI in a way that lets us modify and extend without waiting on them, passing features back and forth with their library.
FL-186.walk: Upgrade the Pydantic AI dependency; the Harness's own additions keep working and the new upstream features are usable.
FL-186.observed: Upgraded Pydantic AI and slim from 2.70.0 to 2.71.0 and its harness from 0.70.0 to 0.71.0 in a disposable environment. All 136 agent/tool tests passed. The live tool inventory and skill walk used the newer versions.

FL-192.label: Swappable seams: router, model policy with an off-switch, toolset as a unit, memory system.
FL-192.walk: Change the toolset in config to a different one as a unit; the next thread's agent has that toolset's tools.
FL-192.observed: Saved the alternate toolset and opened a new thread. Its inventory showed workspace tools Off with memory tools still available. Restored the original toolset.

FL-193.label: The common core of terminal-agent tools (skills, progressive prompting, model switching, compaction, app interactions) in one piece that pulls upstream updates.
FL-193.walk: Update the shared core-tools piece to its newest upstream version; skills, model switching and the rest keep working in the Harness.
FL-193.observed: Upgraded the upstream tool pack, ran 136 agent/tool tests and exercised the skill in a live thread. Switching between distinct models was not exercised under the single-model charge.

FL-206.label: Strategies and models: the strategies rail beside the model list, each strategy with its one-sentence meaning and the model it picks now; one plain summary of the model in use; the strategy named wherever the model is.
FL-206.walk: Open the Model Device from the conversation's model chip: the strategies (Pinned, Max, Elbow, Floor, Budget once the ledger has a burn, Local when offline) stand beside the ranked model list, each with what it means and the model it picks now, the one in force marked; the model in use has one paragraph naming its price in and out (the price the chip quotes), context, rank, thinking level, which strategy chose it and why, and since when. Click Elbow; a new thread's header chip, thread-list row, conversation configuration legend and spend-module model row all read 'Elbow · <model>'. Pick Floor and Budget from the rail the same way.
FL-206.observed: Opened the Model Device and inspected its active mini policy. Following Elbow, Floor and Budget into new chats with their selected models exceeded the verified single-model scope.

FL-215.label: A button says what it does and one symbol means one thing: one word per action and one icon per meaning, held in two tables in the kit; a confirmation names the action, the thing and what is lost and answers Yes or No. Errors name the failure and a next step while preserving authored guidance; an empty state says what fills it; long instructions and legends open on demand.
FL-215.walk: Open the app. Sending is Send; X removes or closes; Deny wears the barred circle and Approve the check. Archive a thread, Reset a layout and delete a memory: each question names what is lost and offers bare Yes/No. Archiving… stays visible while busy. Import malformed recipe/plugin JSON and interrupt a read: the message names the failure and recovery, never diagnostics. Preserve an authored refusal and a repeated /remember response. Inspect empty modules for one line saying what fills them; open Roots' Legend and the creation scoring legend. Continue, Wrong and Never remain owner-pending under F240.
FL-215.observed: Opened the archive confirmation, inspected its explanation and dismissed it. The destructive actions, error recovery and complete copy matrix remain unproven. Continue, Wrong and Never already await the owner under F240.
